headline: April CPI Accelerates to 2.8% on Record 28.6% Gasoline Spike as BoC Holds at 2.25%
executive_summary:
Canada's headline Consumer Price Index rose +2.8% year-over-year in April 2026, the fastest pace in roughly two years and up from +2.4% in March, driven by a record +28.6% year-over-year increase in gasoline prices, according to Statistics Canada.88 Core CPI on the median-and-trim basis eased to 2.1% from 2.3%, and CPI excluding gasoline slowed to +2.0%, indicating the acceleration was concentrated in energy. The gasoline pass-through tracks WTI crude at US$103.02/bbl amid the Strait of Hormuz disruption; the project database links 672 projects ($141.71B) to fuel-cost dynamics, including 59 oil_gas projects ($97.58B) and 613 transport_logistics projects ($44.13B).88

The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25%32 on April 29, 2026, a fourth consecutive hold, citing the Middle East war and U.S. tariff uncertainty and stating it would not let higher energy prices become persistent inflation. The hold leaves financing conditions steady for 211 residential projects ($32.23B) and 1,678 infrastructure projects ($210.26B) the database flags as rate-sensitive. Real GDP contracted -0.6% annualized in Q4 202584; full-year 2025 growth was +1.7%, the slowest since 2020, with a Q1 2026 advance estimate of +0.4% ahead of the official May 29 release.85

The April Labour Force Survey recorded unemployment rising +0.2 percentage points to 6.9%87 as employment fell -18,000, with youth (15-24) unemployment at 14.3% and the long-term unemployed share at 22.5%. Construction employment fell -16,000 and information, culture and recreation fell -25,000, while health care added +18,000. Canada posted a +C$1.8B merchandise trade surplus in March86, the first since September 2025, as exports rose +8.5% to C$72.8B (energy +15.6%, crude +18.9%, metals and minerals +24%) while imports fell -1.6%; the surplus with the United States widened to C$7.1B. The export-led surplus aligns with 59 oil_gas projects ($97.58B) and 390 mining projects ($227.11B) the database tracks.

Canadian housing starts jumped +17% in April to a 279,317 SAAR from 239,747 in March57, exceeding a roughly 240,000 estimate, with Toronto starts up +34% year-over-year and Montreal +21%. The database links the rebound to 211 residential projects ($32.23B) and 72 NAICS-23 construction projects ($9.96B). Statistics Canada's official Q1 2026 GDP, May labour data, May CPI, and the next Bank of Canada rate decision are scheduled over the coming weeks and will reset the picture.

national.analysis:
Real GDP contracted at an annualized -0.6% in the fourth quarter of 2025, with full-year 2025 growth of +1.7%, the slowest annual pace since 2020, according to Statistics Canada.84 A Q1 2026 advance estimate places growth at +0.4%; the official Q1 release is scheduled for May 29, 2026.85 Inventory withdrawal and weak exports were the principal Q4 drags. By industry, manufacturing GDP fell -3.1% year-over-year (StatCan NAICS 31-33), against which the database tracks 38 manufacturing projects ($62.19B). Management of companies and enterprises (NAICS 55) declined -22.3% year-over-year, while transportation and warehousing (NAICS 48-49) rose +4.5% and mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction (NAICS 21) rose +3.6%.

The April Labour Force Survey recorded unemployment at 6.9%87, up +0.2 percentage points from March, as employment fell -18,000 (-0.1%). The participation rate held near 65.0% and the employment rate was 60.5%. Youth (15-24) unemployment rose +0.5 percentage points to 14.3%, and the long-term unemployed share reached 22.5%. Construction employment fell -16,000 and information, culture and recreation fell -25,000, while health care added +18,000. Manufacturing employment was 244,400 (-2.1% month-over-month). Wage growth ran +3.9% year-over-year on the most recent SEPH reference.

Headline CPI rose +2.8% year-over-year in April88, up from +2.4% in March, led by a record +28.6% gasoline increase. Core CPI (median-and-trim) eased to 2.1% and CPI excluding gasoline slowed to +2.0%. Shelter CPI was +3.6% and food CPI +3.5%. Canadian housing starts jumped +17% in April to a 279,317 SAAR from 239,747 in March57, exceeding a roughly 240,000 estimate, with Toronto starts up +34% year-over-year and Montreal +21%, multi-unit driven; the six-month trend rose +3.2% to 256,777. Construction GDP was -0.5% month-over-month and +2.8% year-over-year. Canada recorded a +C$1.8B merchandise trade surplus in March86, the first since September 2025, as exports rose +8.5% to C$72.8B (energy +15.6%, crude +18.9%, metals and minerals +24%) while imports fell -1.6%; the surplus with the United States widened to C$7.1B. The 2025 IEEPA tariffs ended following a February 2026 U.S. Supreme Court ruling. The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25%32 on April 29, a fourth consecutive hold, with the prime rate at 6.09%; the database links the hold to 211 residential projects ($32.23B) and 1,678 infrastructure projects ($210.26B) flagged as rate-sensitive. The export-led trade surplus, with energy up 15.6% and metals and minerals up 24%, aligns with 59 oil_gas projects ($97.58B) and 390 mining projects ($227.11B), while the record gasoline pass-through tracks WTI crude at US$103.02/bbl and links 672 projects ($141.71B) across the oil_gas and transport_logistics pipelines to fuel-cost dynamics.

global.analysis:
The Federal Reserve held the federal funds target at 3.50%-3.75% on April 29, 2026, in an 8-4 split that marked the most dissents since October 1992, in what was likely Chair Powell's final meeting.58 March U.S. CPI ran +3.3% year-over-year with core at +2.6%; the FOMC statement attributed elevated inflation partly to higher global energy prices. U.S. GDP was +2.0% in Q4 2025 and unemployment 4.3% in March. Markets price the range holding through year-end, with the Kevin Warsh appointment effective May 15, 2026.

The wide Fed-BoC gap — U.S. 3.50%-3.75% against Canada 2.25% — supports the U.S. dollar and caps the Canadian dollar at 0.7264. Higher U.S. Treasury yields lift Government of Canada yields, contributing to the observed bear-steepening with the GoC 2-year at 3.07% and the 10-year at 3.70%, and pressure gold prices.

China's Q1 2026 GDP rose +5.0% year-over-year, up from +4.5% in Q4 2025, reversing the late-2025 slowdown on strong industrial output and an export surge that held up despite the Iran war.56 China halting sulfuric-acid exports from May tightened the global copper supply chain. Rebounding Chinese demand was a primary driver of the copper advance toward a record near US$6.58/lb on May 12.68

Resilient Chinese demand supports copper at US$6.32/lb (+36.21% year-over-year), iron ore, and energy export prices, reinforcing the pipeline's 390 Canadian mining projects ($227.11B). Potash and canola export channels are relevant qualitatively, though no timeseries deltas are available for those commodities this cycle.

The European Central Bank held its three key rates on April 30, 2026, leaving the deposit rate at 2.00%, and described upside inflation and downside growth risks as having intensified.60 A Bloomberg survey indicated expectations of two 25-basis-point ECB increases, in June and September, as the Iran war lifts inflation.38 The energy-driven global inflation regime reinforced the back-up in global term premia.

Higher European energy-driven inflation and potential ECB tightening support the euro and global yields, reinforcing the Government of Canada yield back-up and the global commodity prices Canada exports. The GoC curve showed the 2-year at 3.07% and the long bond at 4.02%, both well above the 2.25% Canadian policy rate, consistent with the cross-border term-premium move.

goodsIndustries.name: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing & Hunting
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Goods-producing industries grew 0.4% in February 2026; agriculture is not separately broken out in the StatCan headline102. Wheat traded at 671.75 on 2026-05-19, up 13.6% versus roughly one month prior, while canola sat at 733.20 CAD/t on a level-only basis with no computable monthly delta per the data gap report100. Lumber traded at 593.00, up 1.7% over the month100. Canola production for 2025 reached 21.8 million tonnes, up 13.3% year-over-year, while 2024 realized net farm income was $9.4 billion, down 26.0% year-over-year25.

China is lowering tariffs on Canadian canola seed to a combined 15% from 84% by 2026-03-01 and removing tariffs on canola meal and peas through end-20266. A Section 232 measure applies a 10% duty on Canadian timber and lumber from October, with cabinets and vanities at 25%, scheduled to rise to 50% on 2027-01-016. Canada added a $500M BDC Softwood Lumber Guarantee plus a $500M Large Enterprise Tariff Loan facility6. The project database tracks 13 sector-tagged projects (~$4.74B), forestry- and pulp-mill-weighted, including the Saint John Pulp Mill Upgrades ($1.10B NB) and Hinton Pulp Mill Expansion ($0.58B AB)26. If China's canola tariff reduction holds through end-2026 and Section 232 softwood duties rise in January 2027, sector exposure shifts toward crop exports and away from forest products.

The goods-exports gain of 8.5% month-over-month aligns with the 22 new manufacturing-tagged projects since 2026-05-122,3. If Ford's Becancour and Port Colborne facilities proceed while Honda Alliston stays suspended, the EV-supply-chain component of the $129.01B pipeline contracts while machinery and durable-goods strength continues per the February print.

industry_executive_summary:
The StatCan GDP-by-industry table shows the goods-producing aggregate up +0.4% in February 2026 before easing in the March advance estimate, with manufacturing leading at +1.8% month-over-month, its largest monthly gain since January 2023, while construction slipped -0.5% and utilities were flat.102 On a year-over-year basis the picture diverges: manufacturing contracted -3.1% and management of companies and enterprises fell -22.3%, the steepest decline among the 20 NAICS industries, while transportation and warehousing rose +4.5%, mining, quarrying and oil-and-gas extraction +3.6%, agriculture +3.5%, and accommodation and food services +3.1%.102

The project database links these movements to physical pipelines. Manufacturing's year-over-year contraction spans 38 sector-tagged projects (~$129.01B in the briefing's broader roll-up), including Honda's C$15B Alliston EV and battery hub recorded as Cancelled across four variants.25 Mining and oil-and-gas extraction carries the largest goods pipeline at 448 sector-tagged projects (~$324.69B), with 38 added since 2026-05-12, anchored by LNG Canada.25 Transportation and warehousing tracks 612 projects ($44.13B), the largest single-week addition at 145 records, led by the $1.16B Contrecoeur container terminal loan.25 Services-side, finance and insurance posted Big Six Q1 FY2026 profit near $19B versus about $14B a year earlier, and public administration ($82.48B across 207 projects) reflects a confirmed federal reduction of roughly 40,000 positions by 2029.25 Industries without dedicated pipelines (wholesale, retail, NAICS 52, 54, 55, 81) are tracked through GDP, labour and earnings series, as industry_gdp.json is empty for all 20 industries this cycle.102

consumer_pulse:
Cost-of-living discussion this cycle centred on record gasoline inflation, with gasoline up +28.6% year-over-year in April88 the dominant sentiment driver. Reddit and Google Trends signals tracked by the pipeline showed "gas prices," "pump pain," and "affordability crisis" as the highest-frequency negative-sentiment topics, alongside "cost of living" and "grocery prices." Food CPI ran +3.5% and rent CPI +3.6%88, sustaining grocery- and rent-affordability themes; food-bank-demand and household-debt topics carried negative sentiment scores in the word-cloud data.

Labour-market softness deepened the negative tone: the April Labour Force Survey recorded unemployment at 6.9% and youth unemployment at 14.3%87, with private-sector job losses tracked at roughly 112,000 year-to-date in 2026. "Unemployment rising," "private-sector layoffs," and "youth jobs" registered among the most frequent topics. Oil-shock anxiety tied to the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz disruption surfaced repeatedly, as did recession-fear and Q4 GDP-contraction discussion.

Lower-intensity topics carried mixed sentiment. The federal affordability response — a fuel excise suspension to September 7 and the Groceries and Essentials Benefit — appeared with mildly positive sentiment, as did the April housing-starts rebound and the March trade surplus. The Bank of Canada hold and the TSX level registered neutral. E-commerce and retail discussion aligned with retail trade GDP at +2.3% year-over-year88 against elevated transport-cost commentary linked to diesel and fuel prices.

marketCommentary:
Canadian equities and the loonie eased while energy markets extended a war-driven rally in the week ending May 15 — the S&P/TSX Composite fell -0.72% to 33,83313, and the Canadian dollar weakened -0.64% to 0.7264 CAD/USD, against the 125-basis-point gap between the Federal Reserve's 3.50%-3.75% target and the Bank of Canada's 2.25% policy rate3258. WTI crude held at US$103.02/bbl, up +64.33% year-over-year amid the Strait of Hormuz disruption61, while copper traded at US$6.32/lb (+36.21% YoY)68. The project database tracks $1,472.2 billion across 7,482 active and proposed projects13.

The pipeline's exposure splits between rate-sensitive and commodity-linked segments — the database contains 211 residential projects ($32.23B) and 1,678 infrastructure projects ($210.26B), a combined $242.49 billion carrying financing-cost exposure to a yield curve that bear-steepened to a 3.07% 2-year and 3.70% 10-year, both well above the overnight rate32. On the commodity side, 59 oil_gas projects ($97.58B) and 613 transport_logistics projects ($44.13B) are tied to fuel-cost dynamics, while 390 mining projects ($227.11B) align with copper strength68. If WTI holds above US$100, the 672 fuel-exposed projects ($141.71B) would continue to face elevated input costs88.

yieldCurveCommentary: The Government of Canada curve held a normal, upward slope, with the 2Y at 3.07% and the 10Y at 3.70% for a 2s10s spread of about 63 basis points — little changed from the roughly 64 basis points a year ago, with the entire curve well above the 2.25% overnight rate as global term-premium repricing met an energy-driven inflation regime88. Prior-week levels were unavailable, so moves are measured against year-ago levels: the 2Y is up about 54 basis points from 2.53% and the 10Y up about 53 basis points from 3.17%, with the Long bond up roughly 55 basis points to 4.02%, the highest level on the curve. The Bank of Canada's fourth consecutive hold at 2.25% on April 29 anchored the front end while ECB tightening expectations and the Bank of England's third consecutive no-cut decision pushed the global long end higher326033. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the rate path to 1,678 infrastructure projects valued at $210.26B and 211 residential projects valued at $32.23B carrying rate-sensitive financing exposure. If the yields tracked here hold near current levels rather than retreating toward the policy rate, those projects, totalling roughly $242.49B in tracked value, would carry financing costs consistent with term yields more than a full point above the held overnight rate rather than the lower yields seen a year earlier32.
